subject: Request: Change order to split order form fee across ledgers and add capacity
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <amonroe@ledgercorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: finance+procurement@ledgercorp.com
Date: 2028-06-01 09:12 PDT
Subject: Change order request: split fee allocation + add 40% burst capacity

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LedgerCorp is ready to move forward but we need one commercial tweak before procurement can sign. Our finance team needs the order form fee to be split across two internal ledgers (R&D and Production) for FY29 budgeting, and we also want to add a temporary 40% burst capacity for Q3 (expected Jul-Sep).

I've attached a short proposal that shows the ledger split and a redline of the order form with suggested fee apportionment. Can Redwood produce a change order (or amendment to the MSA/order form) that: 
- Reflects the fee split (60% Production / 40% R&D) with corresponding invoicing schedule
- Adds a one-time capacity supplement for Q3 with prorated fees
- Includes any tax/e-invoicing info we need to provide for the ledger mapping

Procurement is on a tight cadence — can you confirm if this needs legal redlines vs. a standard change order template? I can loop in our AP contact if that helps.

Attachments: LedgerCorp_SOW_Split_Proposal_v1.pdf, OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx, tax-ledger-mapping.xlsx

Appreciate a quick confirmation.

Best,
Alex
Head of Procurement
LedgerCorp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <amonroe@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01 10:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Change order request: split fee allocation + add 40% burst capacity

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the files. Confirming we can support ledger-level invoicing and a Q3 burst addendum, but we do need to run the redlines through Legal for any MSA-level language changes (payment routing, invoicing clause, tax treatment).

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll prepare a draft change order template that handles the capacity supplement as a timeboxed exhibit and the fee apportionment as invoice instructions.
2) Karthik — can you surface any commercial constraints (minimums, billing cadence changes) we should call out before Legal drafts?
3) Laura — can you coordinate with Legal to confirm whether the MSA needs an amendment or if the Order Form can carry the invoicing instructions?

Alex, expect a draft by EOD tomorrow (6/2) with options: (A) Order Form exhibit only, (B) Order Form + MSA amendment language. If Procurement has a preferred path let me know.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee | Sr. Sales Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-01 11:48 PDT
Subject: Re: Change order request: split fee allocation + add 40% burst capacity

Quick commercial note: we can do the 40% burst as a fixed temporary top-up (prorated by days active) or as an optional burst pool billed on consumption. For procurement simplicity they usually prefer fixed top-ups (predictable invoice).

A few things Legal will want to review/confirm before we send back to LedgerCorp:
- Whether splitting invoicing across two ledgers triggers any third-party billing restrictions (some customers require a single legal entity invoice)
- Whether the fee apportionment requires an updated payment instruction appendix (bank details, tax IDs)
- If we put the burst in an exhibit, ensure there is a clear end date and automatic reversion to baseline capacity

Assume pricing for the top-up uses the same per-token tiers unless Legal flags a need for a separate fee table.

I'll be available for a short call 1:30–2:00pm PT if helpful.

—Karthik
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Alex Monroe <amonroe@ledgercorp.com>
Date: 2028-06-02 09:34 PDT
Subject: Fwd: Change order request: split fee allocation + add 40% burst capacity

Forwarding to Legal and Finance ops with our initial take.

Team, tagging FinanceOps (Connor) — see attached ledger mapping. Legal: propose we do the following draft approach and ask for redline guidance: 
1) Order Form Exhibit A (Ledger Allocation): 
   - Inserted table that shows fee split 60/40, invoice counters for each ledger, and invoice schedule (monthly AR run).
   - Billing address and tax ID mapping appendix attached (tax-ledger-mapping.xlsx).
2) Capacity Addendum (timeboxed exhibit): 
   - One-time capacity supplement from 2028-07-01 to 2028-09-30. Fixed fee calculated as prorated units; reverts automatically post period.
3) Payment & Invoicing clause: 
   - If the customer requires multiple invoices, add clause that Redwood will issue separate invoices to designated ledgers provided by the customer and is not responsible for internal ledger reconciliations.

Legal questions for redline: 
- Does splitting invoices across ledgers create a need to amend the MSA payment language (currently single payer wording)?
- Any required tax disclosures or evidence we need to collect for cross-ledger invoicing?

Alex — if that approach looks right I will circulate a draft change order + exhibit for your review by EOD today.

Laura Bennett
Director, Contracts & Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: tax-ledger-mapping.xlsx

From: Alex Monroe <amonroe@ledgercorp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-03 16:44 PDT
Subject: Re: Change order request: split fee allocation + add 40% burst capacity

Thanks Laura — that plan looks good. A couple clarifications from our side before you draft: 
- Ledger IDs: see sheet — please populate the "Bill To" fields exactly as shown so our AP can auto-route.
- We prefer the fixed top-up for Q3. Please include a short note that any unused portion of the top-up is non-refundable but can be converted to overage credits if both parties agree in writing.
- DocuSign: procurement will need a single envelope with two signers (LedgerCorp PO signer + Redwood signer). We can accept multiple invoice recipients within the envelope.

If you can circulate the draft change order + exhibits today we'll route on our side and aim to sign by 6/7. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Alex
